prompt: A museum gift shop can stock either more varieties of postcards or deeper quantities of its most popular designs. Discuss how it could choose. Use approximately 80 words for the response.
text: The shop should compare sales data, visitor preferences, profit margins, and storage costs. More varieties may appeal to diverse tastes and showcase more of the museum’s collection, but slow-selling designs can tie up money and space. Deeper stocks of popular postcards reduce stockouts and may secure bulk discounts, though limited choice could disappoint visitors. A balanced approach is to maintain strong supplies of bestsellers while testing smaller quantities of new designs, then adjust the mix using sales results and customer feedback.
